title: AI Evaluation & Benchmarking
description: Create datasets to test if an AI prompt actually works. Tests "LLM-as-a-judge" concepts, test-case creation, and scoring rubrics.

seo.overviewBody: Rigorous evaluation guarantees AI applications maintain quality in production. AI QA engineers evaluate LLM applications using LLM-as-a-Judge methodologies, RAG Triad metrics (Context Relevance, Groundedness, Answer Relevance), scoring rubrics, and automated test datasets.

deliverables.title: 1. LLM Evaluation Rubric & Scoring Matrix
deliverables.desc: Multi-dimensional scoring rubric evaluating accuracy, tone, compliance, completeness, and hallucination rates.

deliverables.title: 2. Automated LLM-as-a-Judge Test Suite
deliverables.desc: Python test script using a powerful evaluator LLM (e.g. GPT-4o) to grade application responses against ground-truth datasets.

deliverables.title: 3. RAG Triad Performance Benchmark Report
deliverables.desc: Benchmark report evaluating Context Relevance, Groundedness (Faithfulness), and Answer Relevance scores.

faqs.question: What is the LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation methodology?
faqs.answer: Using a high-capability LLM (like GPT-4o or Claude 3.5 Sonnet) as an automated evaluator to grade candidate model outputs against structured scoring rubrics and reference answers.

faqs.question: What are the 3 metrics of the RAG Triad?
faqs.answer: 1. Context Relevance (was retrieved context relevant to query?), 2. Groundedness / Faithfulness (is the answer derived solely from retrieved context?), 3. Answer Relevance (does the answer directly address the user query?).

faqs.question: How do you detect hallucinations programmatically?
faqs.answer: Compare claims in the model's output against facts in the retrieved context using NLI (Natural Language Inference) premise-entailment verification.
